answer: The saving comes from a per-level recurrence. A call at parameter mf splits its data into W streams of volume V/W and makes s smaller calls on them, where s is the total rank of the edge changes and each unit of rank is one smaller call. Writing C(f) for the time per unit volume at parameter f, the children cost s(V/W)C(f), so C(mf) <= (s/W)C(f) + O(1) with C(1) = O(1) (pipozop). Unrolling over the log_m f levels gives C(f) = O(sum_j (s/W)^j). If s/W < m^tau with a fixed tau < 1, the sum is O(f^tau), so an interchange costs O(V f^tau) (pipozop). For the bit network tau = 1 - 2^-50. The strict inequality s < Wm is what makes a tau < 1 available: the per-level factor s/W must be below the factor m by which the parameter shrinks. Pukezad gives s_b = Wm - (N - 2L_b) with L_b/N = 100/539 < 1/2, so the deficit N - 2L_b is positive (pukezad). Pipozop turns that deficit into a margin: s/W = m(1 - eta) with eta = 339/(22587335 m), about 1.5e-11, and the exponential estimate m^(1-2^-50) > m(1 - 20*2^-50) > m(1 - eta) = s/W holds because ln m < 20 and eta exceeds 20*2^-50 (pipozop). So the one strict inequality gives an exponent strictly below 1 by a small positive amount. Gap in the pages, which is my own reconstruction and not stated on any page: with s = Wm exactly, the unrolled sum is about sum_j m^j = O(f), i.e. linear, so no saving; the exponent of the last term is log_m(s/W), which is below 1 exactly when s/W < m.

I am less sure of the rank count s = Wm - (N - 2L_b), which I took on the word of the Pukezad page without checking the network.
